transcript.content: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is I’m having a harder time keeping my mind on one thing than I’d like to admit. I’m a carpenter, and lately one saw starting up, or somebody walking past the office, or even just a thought about another job can pull me off what I’m doing. Then I look up and somehow the whole day’s gotten away from me. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been… more of a problem than I can really brush off now.
When you think back to childhood, were you already having trouble staying focused then?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I was a terrible student or anything—I did okay in some ways. But even in grade school, before I was 12, my teachers would tell my mother I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, forget what the instructions were, or just kind of stare out the window instead of finishing my work at my desk.  

At the time I think everybody just thought I needed to try harder. Does that answer what you mean?
Does this difficulty focusing also happen outside of work?

Yes… I mean, it’s not only at work. Work is just where it’s most obvious, because there’s so much going on. But even outside of that, my mind gets pulled off pretty easily.

Like, if there’s a noise or someone moving around, or even just a thought about something else I should be doing, I’ll lose the thread of what I was doing. Then I’ll realize a lot of time has passed and I didn’t really stay with the thing I meant to. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it does feel like I can’t keep my mind on one thing the way I used to. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed this becoming worse recently compared with how it usually was for you?

Yeah… I think it has been worse recently. Not overnight, exactly, but this level of trouble has probably been going on about a year or so—maybe a year and a month.

It seemed to start after I broke my wrist and got moved off the hands-on carpentry for a while, more into shop paperwork and supervising. I’m not saying I was perfect before that, but since then it’s been a lot harder to keep myself on track. Does that sound like the kind of timeline you mean?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Um… I don’t think so. Not depressed, exactly. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling really down in that way.

At least, I haven’t noticed that as the main thing. Is that what you mean?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an obvious reason to?

I don’t think so… not in a constant way, anyway. I mean, I worry about normal things, like if I’ve missed something or if I’m behind, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around anxious for no reason.

At least, I haven’t noticed that being the main problem. Does that answer it okay?
Do you feel this worsening in focus began because of the stress of your wrist injury and the change in your job?

I think… yes, that’s when I really noticed it. I don’t want to blame everything on the wrist, exactly, but after I broke it and got shifted away from the hands-on carpentry into more paperwork and supervising, this level of trouble started showing up.

It’s been about a year and a month like this, more or less. Does that make sense?
Do you often feel restless, like it’s hard to sit still?

Yeah… I guess I do, some. I try not to make a big deal of it, but when I’m stuck at the desk doing estimates, or in a long meeting, I feel kind of wound up inside—like I need to get up and move around.

I know I’m supposed to just sit there and finish, and my wrist is healed now, so it’s not that. It’s more like I just feel… restless, I guess. Does that sound like what you’re asking?
When your attention drifts, do you find yourself getting pulled into vivid daydreams or fantasies?

Not really like fantasies, no… I don’t think I’m sitting there imagining some whole other life or anything.

It’s more that my attention gets pulled off by anything. Like if a saw starts up, or somebody walks past the office, or I suddenly think about another job I’m supposed to check on, then I’m off track. And then I look up and half the day’s gone and I haven’t stayed with the one thing I meant to do.

I don’t know if that’s what you mean by daydreaming, but that’s more what it feels like for me.
Has this trouble staying focused been causing problems at home?

At home… yeah, it has, though I hate saying that. I try to keep it together, but my husband’s had to take over more of the bills and reminding me about things because I’ll misplace papers or miss something that needed to get done.

And it’s not just home, honestly. At work, when I make mistakes or take too long, it’s cost me commissions and caused rework, and the crew doesn’t seem as willing to depend on me for scheduling or ordering anymore. I’m embarrassed about it, but yes, it’s causing problems.
When you’re doing something you really enjoy, do you still have trouble keeping your attention on it?

Even if it’s something I like, I can still get pulled off, yeah. I wish I could say it’s only the boring stuff, but… one saw starts up, or someone walks past the office, or I suddenly remember another job I need to check on, and my mind just goes with it.

Then I’ll realize I didn’t stay with the one thing I meant to do, and a whole chunk of the day is gone. I don’t mean to make it sound dramatic, but that’s kind of what brings me in.
When you try to read something, do you often have to go back and reread it because your mind drifted off?

Yeah… I do. I mean, not every single thing, but often enough that it’s a problem.

I’ll read a paragraph and realize I didn’t really take it in because my mind jumped somewhere else — a saw starting up, someone walking by, or even just a thought about another job I’m supposed to check on. Then I have to go back and read it again.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but that’s really what brings me in… I just can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing, and then the day gets away from me.
When you’re back doing hands-on carpentry, is it easier for you to stay focused?

A little, maybe, because my hands are busy and I know the work. I don’t want to overstate it.

But honestly, even then I can still get pulled off. One saw starts up, or somebody walks past, or I suddenly think about another job I need to check on, and then I’m not with what I was doing anymore. That’s really what brings me in… I just can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing, and then the day gets away from me.
Outside of work, do you still have the same trouble staying focused?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say it’s just work because that’s where there’s so much going on, but it does happen outside of work too.

It’s the same kind of thing, really — I’ll be trying to keep my mind on one thing, and then something small pulls me away, or I’ll think of something else I should be doing, and before I know it I’m off track. I don’t mean to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s the part that worries me… it feels like I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore, and then time gets away from me.
Do you often interrupt other people before they’ve finished speaking?

I don’t think so… not often, anyway.

I mean, I might jump in once in a while if I think I know what someone is going to say, but I don’t think people would describe me as always cutting them off. At least I hope not. If that’s something you mean in a more specific way, I can think about it, but it’s not one of the main things I’ve noticed.
Do you often have trouble getting organized for tasks, like keeping papers, tools, or steps in order?

Yes… yeah, I do. I mean, I try to keep it together, but since I’ve been stuck doing more of the shop paperwork, it’s been pretty obvious.

I’ll have bids, schedules, invoices, and then somebody asking me apprentice questions, and I just… I can’t seem to sort out what needs to happen first. It all ends up piled on my bench, and then I’m rushing to catch up, and still missing deadlines sometimes.

I don’t like saying that, because I feel like I should be better at it by now, but that’s been happening.
As a child, did these attention problems get you into trouble both at school and at home?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I wasn’t trying to cause trouble.

But even in grade school — definitely before I was 12 — my teachers would tell my mother things like I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, or forget what the instructions were, or I’d be looking out the window instead of finishing the work at my desk.

At home it was sort of the same concern coming back from school, if that makes sense. My mom would hear about it, and I’d get talked to for not paying attention or not doing what I was supposed to. I guess I kind of thought that was normal at the time.
When this happens, do you ever feel detached from yourself or like things around you aren’t quite real?

No… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of feeling outside my body or like the room isn’t real.

Sometimes I get overwhelmed or kind of blank for a minute, but I wouldn’t describe it as detached exactly. I mean, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean? I don’t think that’s really something I’ve noticed.

Yeah… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound like I was a bad kid or anything, because I wasn’t trying to cause trouble.

But even in grade school — definitely before I was 12 — my teachers would tell my mother things like I was bright but careless. I’d lose homework, or forget what the instructions were, or I’d be looking out the window instead of finishing the work at my desk.

At home it was sort of the same concern coming back from school, if that makes sense. My mom would hear about it, and I’d get talked to for not paying attention or not doing what I was supposed to. I guess I kind of thought that was normal at the time.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the concentration problem occurs specifically during dissociative episodes such as feeling unreal or detached, which would support an other dissociative/conversion disorder over ADHD or a stress-related condition.
doctor.question: When this happens, do you ever feel detached from yourself or like things around you aren’t quite real?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feelings of detachment from oneself or unreality of surroundings, which relates to dissociation/depersonalization or derealization and is not covered by the provided ADHD symptom profile items.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. Not in the sense of feeling outside my body or like the room isn’t real.

Sometimes I get overwhelmed or kind of blank for a minute, but I wouldn’t describe it as detached exactly. I mean, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean? I don’t think that’s really something I’ve noticed.

inference.note: Chronic inattention since childhood across school/home and now across work/home, plus restlessness and disorganization, strongly supports ADHD predominantly inattentive presentation. Derealization/depersonalization symptoms denied, arguing against F48.8, and symptoms are not primarily anxiety/depression or a stress reaction, making F43.9 unlikely despite situational worsening after the wrist injury/job change.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking psychiatric care today
opening_question.question: Hello, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a longstanding pattern of attention dysregulation beginning before age 12 and occurring across school, home, work, and current home settings, with clear functional impairment. Confirmed symptoms include distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention, careless mistakes/loss of materials, rereading due to mind-wandering, disorganization, and some restlessness. Mood, generalized anxiety, dissociative symptoms, and fantasy/daydream absorption were not supported as primary explanations. Recent worsening after occupational change appears to exacerbate, not fully account for, a childhood-onset ADHD syndrome.
